We are seeking applications for a Facilities Manager (NSW) to join and lead our Facility Management teams, on a permanent full-time basis.

This position will operate across both Burwood and Richmond Hospitals.

The purpose of this role is to ensure the two NSW psychiatric hospitals, at Burwood and Richmond, continue to operate through meeting all regulatory and legislative requirements of a health care facility and by ensuring all buildings, plant and equipment and surrounding environment are effective and operational.

Leading two high performing teams that maintain day to day oversight of each hospital maintenance, the role also encompasses the management of programmes to ensure the effectiveness of the Hospital sites, while creating efficiencies and cost savings through technological and environmental changes.

The Position

Develop, implement and maintain hospital preventative maintenance programs.

Maintenance, updating and further development of Building Management Systems.

Management of capital works programs as required including new initiatives and replacement planning.

Ensure compliance with relevant statutory standards and regulations.

Maintain up to date records of equipment.

Ensure a cost-effective maintenance services.

Monitoring and review invoicing and service sheets for contracted services to ensure accuracy and value for money.

Develop and maintain an up-to-date capitol replacement life cycle plan to make recommendations to finance as required.

Timely and appropriate management and allocation of staff resources. 

Responsible for the management of staff rosters including management of leave provisions, on-call rostering and allocation of team responsibilities.

We are looking for an experienced professional with a strong background in facility management within a commercial, hospital, or healthcare environment. You will bring proven experience coordinating and managing the day-to-day logistics and operational requirements of a healthcare facility, alongside a positive, adaptable approach and the ability to perform effectively under pressure.

Strong time management, attention to detail, and the ability to prioritise competing demands are essential, along with proficiency in standard office software and engineering works management systems.

Lead day-to-day patient flow and performance reporting while driving strategic service improvement, developing contemporary clinical access procedures, and providing operational leadership to the NSLHD Mental Health Line to ensure consumers receive the right care, at the right time, in the right place.

Employment Type: Temporary Part Time until 1 August 2027 (with possibility of ongoing employment)

Requisition ID: REQ677691

Who we are: We are a health service that touches thousands of lives across the Northern Sydney Local Health District, together as a team of like-minded people. We are passionate, driven and have the skills and knowledge to care for our patients whilst creating the best services possible. Our teams have meaningful, interesting and rewarding work everyday. We challenge and nurture each other, sharing our knowledge and experience so that we can deliver better care for everyone There's a real sense of belonging here because we value and respect our patients, employees, and teams' voices. You'll feel a real privilege being a trusted caregiver in our patients, their families, their carers, and our communities' lives. 

NSLHD is proud of our diverse and inclusive workplaces, a place where health care professionals can thrive and feel they belong. We are committed to ensure that all our people feel respected and participate safely within a work environment without aggression, sexual harassment, discrimination and racism.

Where you'll be working

 
Macquarie Hospital

What you'll be doing
The Mental Health Drug and Alcohol (MHDA) Clinical Access and Demand Manager (CADM) is accountable for the safe and effective transition of consumer through Ambulatory, Acute, Rehabilitation and Community based MHDA services. Inclusive of State Network Services such as Mental Health Intensive Care (MHICU) and Children and Youth Mental Health Services (CYMHS) beds and those consumers that require access from within Northern Sydney Local Health District (NSLHD) Acute Facilities to MHDA services. 

Achieved through the application of strong leadership, advanced analytical and negotiation skills working within a collaborative model across a range of stakeholders and people with a lived experience within NSLHD, MHDA Services and external agencies. The role provides leadership and support to the NSLHD Patient and Transfer Unit (PATU) to coordinate MHDA consumer transfers between Hospitals, admissions via community services, and external agencies into NSLHD MHDA services. 

Provides strong collaborative leadership to ensure MHDA Services meet and achieve Key Performance Indicators (KPI) within NSLHD MHDA Services and Ministry of Health (MOH), which includes monitoring and reporting of KPI. 
The position supports directed MHDA National Safety and Quality Health Service Standards (NSQHS). 

The position requires advanced clinical, communication and interpersonal skills which facilitates the ability to work collaboratively within multi-disciplinary teams. That achieve efficient and effective patient flow ensuring MHDA consumers receive the right care at the right time in the right place. The position has line management responsibility MHTAL and reporting of KPI to the MOH and MHDA Services. 

People of Aboriginal and-or Torres Strait Islander background are encouraged to apply.

Candidates will need to meet the following criteria:

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Current Registered Nurse Division 1 with Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) and current NSW Drivers Licence.

A comprehensive understanding of the NSW Health policy framework, priorities and performance indicators and their impact on mental health Patient flow.

Demonstrated high level written, timely and accurate standards of work, complimented by oral communication skills and ability for preparing and presentation of reports to MHDA Executive, NSLH and MOH. Advanced computer skills including Microsoft Office suite of programs, data analysis and patient flow tools such as Electronic Journey Board and Patient Flow Portal.

Ability to work autonomously as well as part of a collaborative team. Highly developed time management, problem solving, negotiation and conflict resolution skills.

Using your advanced clinical expertise, you will lead service development initiatives, provide specialist physiotherapy care for complex patient presentations, and champion evidence-based practice, quality assurance and patient outcome measures. Location: Airport West, VIC 3042
Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Floor Manager
Job Title: Fitter
Salary range: $79,500 - $85,000 + Superannuation – depending on skill level.
Job Closure date:3 0 days

About our client:
Our client, a renowned leader in the automotive repair industry with over three decades of excellence, is seeking a dedicated and meticulous Fitter to join their dynamic team. Renowned for their commitment to precision and restoring vehicles to their pre-accident condition, they operate from a state-of-the-art facility. If you have a passion for automotive craftsmanship and a keen eye for detail, this is your opportunity to contribute to a business that sets the industry standard.

About the Role:
In this pivotal role, you will be responsible for the hands-on structural and panel fitting that forms the foundation of every vehicle restoration. You will work on a variety of vehicles, utilizing advanced equipment and techniques to ensure every repair meets rigorous safety and quality standards. This position is perfect for a technician who takes pride in their work and understands that a perfect fit is the first step to a flawless finish.

Key Duties & Responsibilities:
Vehicle Structure & Frame Analysis:
• Conduct comprehensive inspections of vehicle collision damage to assess structural integrity and identify misalignments in frames, unibody structures, and suspension mounting points.
• Utilize advanced frame straightening equipment and hydraulic systems to meticulously pull and correct structural damage back to the manufacturer’s original specifications.
• Diagnose and perform precise repairs on a vehicle's underlying structure, ensuring its safety and performance are fully restored.

Precision Panel Fitting & Alignment:
• Expertly install, align, and fit a wide range of metal panels, frames, and subassemblies—including doors, fenders, quarter panels, and bumpers—to achieve perfect contours and structural integrity.
• Meticulously adjust all replacement parts to ensure consistent, manufacturer-specified gaps and flushness across the entire vehicle body.
• Modify or custom-fabricate replacement body panels through skilled cutting, grinding, bending, and welding of sheet metal to perfectly match the vehicle's original contours.

Technical Interpretation & Mechanical Fitting:
• Interpret complex technical specifications, detailed vehicle blueprints, and comprehensive collision repair guides to determine the correct materials, tools, and sequences for each unique repair task.
• Perform the fitting and installation of mechanical components such as exhaust systems, fuel lines, and associated brackets, ensuring all parts are securely mounted and functionally sound.

Quality Control & Surface Preparation:
• Employ precision measuring instruments including callipers, micrometres, and specialised alignment tools to verify the accuracy of gaps, contours, and dimensions on all repaired or replaced body parts.
• Prepare vehicle surfaces for refinishing by undertaking skilled sanding, application of body fillers, and priming to create a perfectly smooth substrate, ready for painting.
Equipment Operation & Maintenance:
• Configure and operate a range of specialised workshop machinery, including MIG/MAG welding equipment, frame straighteners, and pneumatic/hydraulic tools, tailoring their settings for specific repair applications.

The Ideal Candidate Will Have:
• A proven track record as a Vehicle Fitter, Panel Beater, or in a similar role within the automotive repair industry.
• Formal qualifications in Automotive Body Repair, Metal Fabrication, or a related trade are highly regarded.
• Proficiency in reading and interpreting technical drawings and repair procedures.
• Demonstrated, hands-on experience with welding, metal fabrication, and the use of precision measuring tools.
• Strong mechanical aptitude and a meticulous approach to every task, with an unwavering commitment to quality.
• The ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a cohesive team in a fast-paced environment.
• A strong commitment to adhering to all workplace health and safety guidelines.

If you are a skilled Fitter ready to take on a rewarding role with a company that values quality and expertise, we encourage you to apply.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

A.B.N. 63 686 723 320

Please include Reference: J1694-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Summary

Our client MICA BROS PTY LTD is seeking to add Welder (First Class) to its specialist wrought iron and architectural metalwork team in Tullamarine, Victoria. The business delivers custom-made gates, staircases, balustrades, decorative ironwork and luxury home features, managing design, fabrication, finishing, delivery and installation in-house with a strong focus on precision, durability and craftsmanship.

The typical job responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:

- Interpret drawings, specifications and work instructions for custom wrought iron projects.
- Measure, mark and prepare steel components for fabrication and installation.
- Perform MIG and TIG welding on mild steel and stainless steel.
- Fabricate wrought iron gates, fences, balustrades, handrails and security doors.
- Cut, shape and form metal sections using appropriate tools and machinery.
- Align and assemble components using clamps, jigs and measuring instruments.
- Complete on-site measurements and modifications to ensure accurate final fitment.
- Inspect welds for strength, penetration, alignment, finish and overall quality.
- Grind, polish, smooth and finish welded joints to required standards.
- Apply safe work practices when handling tools, machinery and metal materials.
- Assist with professional delivery and installation of completed metalwork products.
- Coordinate with builders, supervisors and clients during fabrication and installation stages.
- Maintain fabrication equipment, tools and work areas in safe operating condition.
- Follow Australian Standards, workplace procedures and WHS requirements at all times.
- Support high-quality workmanship across bespoke residential and architectural metalwork projects.

Applicants must meet the following minimum requirements to be considered for the role:

- Certificate IV in Engineering or equivalent welding and fabrication qualification is required for this position.
- At least two years of relevant welding, fabrication or architectural metalwork experience is required.
- Demonstrated MIG and TIG welding experience across mild steel and stainless steel is required.
- Ability to read engineering drawings, technical specifications and fabrication instructions is essential.
- Experience fabricating and installing gates, balustrades, handrails or security doors is highly relevant.
- Strong site measuring, fitting, modification and installation skills are required for custom project work.
- Applicants must demonstrate sound WHS knowledge and safe handling of fabrication tools and machinery.
- High attention to detail and quality finishing skills are required for premium custom metalwork projects.

Please include Reference: J1694-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au
